correctness.rationale: For odd p, Phi_{p^k}(n) is always odd, so a relative tau-number n is square. If a prime r != p divides Phi_{p^k}(n), then ord_r(n)=p^k and r>p. A prime r dividing tau(n) is bounded by one plus an exponent and hence by Omega(n)+1. This yields Omega(n)>=p-1; equality forces one exponent p-1, and Fermat's theorem gives the converse for q != p. The p=2 case is checked directly. The proof has no finite cutoff.
